text:
nina: Quick follow-up after the incident postmortem (INC-2026-03-18). I'm collecting owners for remediation items so we don't lose momentum. Please ack and add any missing blockers.

nina: Summary actions I drafted:
- quota fallback pools: configure a small cross-region spare pool and emergency provider quota request (owner: ajay, ETA: 2026-03-28)
- scheduler policy: add podPriority tweaks + descheduler rule to evict low-priority noise (owner: tom, ETA: 2026-03-24)
- headroom simulation: run synthetic bursts against each cluster to validate headroom % and warm caches (owner: leo, ETA: 2026-04-02)
- autoscale policy: add step-scaling for 30s-5min windows and lower cooldowns (owner: maria, ETA: 2026-03-30)
- telemetry: add "surge_reason" tag and spike-count metric to make regressions visible (owner: nina, ETA: 2026-03-20)
- billing guardrails: add alert when cost-per-token increases >10% during surge (owner: ajay, ETA: 2026-03-27)

ajay: Ack. I'll open emergency quota ticket + long term request. Also adding a provider-agnostic fallback plan doc. Putting ticket link here when created.

tom: Ack. For the descheduler rule I'll prototype a rule to evict <100ms-background jobs first. Will test in canary. Also want to try lowering the eviction grace from 2m -> 20s.

maria: Ack. Autoscale policy change needs to be validated with load runner. I'll coordinate with infra to reserve 3 GPUs on staging for the test window.

leo: For headroom sim, can we start with 20% headroom for prod and 10% for internal clusters? I'll run the replay harness across regions. Need the exact request trace — nina, can you attach the spike trace?

nina: Attached a sanitized spike payload to the postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/INC-2026-03-18/trace-sample. Use the keys: timestamps, req_type, token_count.

maria: Quick question — for autoscale step policy, what's our target reaction time? 30s? If so we need to ensure controller rate limits allow that.

tom: Target 45s for first scale, then follow-up scaling at 2m intervals. We'll instrument controller logs to detect rate-limit backoff.

ajay: Created ticket CP-4555 for emergency quota. Link: https://cloud.vendor/support/CP-4555. Added a checklist: provider contacts, requested SKUs, requested amounts, justification.

ops-bot: Reminder set: "GPU capacity remediation check" starting 2026-03-22 10:00 PT (recurrence: weekly). Assigned to: nina, ajay, maria.

leo: One blocker — network egress limits in eu-west will throttle some fallback pools. We should mark eu-west as constrained and route bursts to us-west first.

nina: Good catch. I'll add eu-west constraint to the runbook and update routing rules.

maria: I pushed a short playbook PR that maps actions -> KPIs: p50 token latency, p95 tail latency, preemption_count, scale_latency, cost_delta. Link: https://git.redwood/internal/runbooks/gpu-surge-playbook/pull/12

tom: Canary plan posted in eng-infra. Config name: surge-canary-v3. I'll start canary 2026-03-24 09:00 PT and tag this thread with results.

ajay: Adding cost guardrail alert to monitoring. Will include runbook steps for emergency scale-down if cost spikes.

nina: Excellent. Next steps: 1) owners confirm (acked), 2) nina adds spike payload + eu-west constraint to postmortem (done) 3) tom runs canary and posts results by 03/25 4) infra reserves staging GPUs for maria by 03/23 5) weekly checks until green. If any ETA slips more than 48h, escalate to eng-sre lead.

leo: One last note — let's record any recurring patterns in the incident tracker (I saw similar preemption blips in Jan). I'll add a short timeline to the tracker.

nina: Thanks — I'll consolidate notes into the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
